newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HKMA says more home loan restraints may be needed.
newsitem.headline: HKMA says more home loan restraints may be needed.

text.p: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) said on Monday additional restraints in mortgage lending policies may be required as growth in lending has resulted in an increase in banks' property exposure.

"The current growth of mortgage lending is historically high and this is resulting in an increase in banks' property exposure. Additional restraint in lending policies may therefore be required," David Carse, deputy chief executive of the HKMA, said in a statement.
The HKMA said gross new loans made during April increased by 35.2 percent to a record high of HK$22.7 billion compared with a drop of 10.6 percent in March.
The average size of new loans also increased to HK$1.77 million from HK$1.47 million.
New loans approved during April rose by 36.4 precent to HK$28.8 billion, reflecting the large scale of market activity in March, it said.
Loans approved but not yet drawn increased by 22.4 percent from HK$14.1 billion in March to HK$17.3 billion in April.
"The rapid growth in new mortgage lending in April was a result of the active property market in March. Market activity slowed in April itself," Carse said.
"However, loan growth seems likely to continue at a rapid pace in May because of the amount of undrawn loan commitments still in the pipeline," he said.
Gross new loans for the purchase of properties in China increased to HK$238 million in April from HK$195 million in March.
The amount of outstanding loans increased by 0.56 percent to HK$6.6 billion, the HKMA said.
